newsitem.title: USA: GM earnings soar to $1.3 billion.
newsitem.headline: GM earnings soar to $1.3 billion.

text.p: General Motors Corp., facing a rancorous strike by its Canadian workers, Tuesday reported a $1.3 billion third-quarter profit as both its North American and international automotive operations registered strong performances.

The world's largest automaker said the combined net income of its North American Automotive Operations and its Delphi Automotive Systems parts businesses was $515 million, the first third-quarter profit for NAO-Delphi since 1986. A year ago, the operations had a combined loss of $93 million, although the parent company posted a profit of $396.7 million.

"The third-quarter results from continuing operations clearly show momentum as we continue to rebuild our strength in North America and grow our business in key international markets throughout the world," Chairman and Chief Executive Officer John Smith said in a statement accompanying the results.
The latest earnings, equal to $1.57 a share, compared with a profit of 39 cents a share from continuing operations. Revenues climbed to $39.1 billion from $35.3 billion in the 1995 period.

The results were boosted by $253 million due to a one-time after-tax gain from a reduction in the automaker's reserve to pay for plant closings. The reduction was required based on the company's decision to use its Wilmington, Del., facility to assemble new Saturn vehicles.
GM said the North American automotive and Delphi parts unit had a net profit margin of 2.1 percent in the quarter, compared with a net loss margin of 0.4 percent in the 1995 quarter.

"We still have our work cut out to improve margin performance," Smith said. "Although we're pleased that the margin did improve year over year, it's still well short of our goal of achieving an average annual net-profit margin of 5 percent over the automotive busines cycle."

Talks between GM's Canadian unit and the union representing the automaker's 26,000 striking Canadian workers were expected to resume this week following a break for the Canadian Thanksgiving long weekend. Bargaining has floundered since the escalating strike began Oct. 2.

The key stumbling block in the talks is GM's ability to shift work outside the company, usually to non-unionized suppliers, a practice known as outsourcing. Analysts said the strong surge in GM's third-quarter results is not expected to make the union any more willing to compromise.

The automaker delivered 1,182,000 vehicles in the United States in the quarter, for a 30.4 percent share of its core market. That was down from 1,235,000 units and a 32.2 percent market share in the year-ago period.

GM's international automotive business contributed net income of $323 million in the period, up from $111 million a year ago. It delivered 792,000 vehicles in the quarter for a 9.1 percent market share, up from 718,000 vehicles and an 8.9 share of the market in the 1995 period.

GM Europe reported third-quarter net income of $75 million, compared with a loss of $98 million a year ago. Income from the rest of the international operations, including Latin America, Asia and the Pacific regions, was $248 million, up from $209 million.
Smith attributed the higher international profits to increased volume and favourable currency rates.

GM's overall profits were helped by an effective income tax rate of 2.8 percent. It said the low rate resulted from favourable resolution of items related to prior-year tax returns, overall foreign tax rates that were lower than the U.S. statutory rate, and reinstatement of research and experimentation credits for the last half of 1996.
The company's General Motors Acceptance Corp. finance unit earned $307 million, compared with $254 million in profits a year ago.
Its Hughes Electronics Corp. unit earned $252 million, down from $256 million in the 1995 period.

The automaker completed the spinoff of its Electronic Data Systems computer services unit on June 7, and the latest results exclude EDS' performance. In the 1995 period, income from the discontinued operations of EDS totalled $246 million.
GM's stock gained $1.375 to $53.25 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
